idiom_name: extension UserDto { init(_ user: User) } + extension User { var dto: UserDto }
implementation_notes: Swift keeps the mapping in an extension dedicated to it: `extension UserDto { init(_ user: User) { ... } }` and `extension User { var dto: UserDto { ... } }`, so the DTO's members are set in one place and neither type's primary declaration knows the other. Value semantics help: the initialiser copies fields and a `let`-only DTO cannot drift after construction; use a named `static func from(_:)` when an initialiser would collide with the memberwise one or when the conversion can fail (`init?`). Codable is the other half of the boundary - it maps the DTO to and from the wire - but it does not translate domain meaning, so the domain-to-DTO step stays hand-written unless the two representations coincide.
pitfalls: An initialiser whose signature mirrors the memberwise initialiser makes overload resolution ambiguous at the call site; prefer `static func from(_:)` when both exist.
Value types copy, but a nested reference type (class, closure) is copied by reference: the DTO can still observe later mutation of shared state.
Failable conversions belong in an `init?` or throwing initialiser rather than a `try!` inside the mapper, which turns bad input into a crash.

variants.name: Codable with custom CodingKeys / init(from:)
variants.idiom_name: Codable conformance with private enum CodingKeys and custom init(from:) / encode(to:)
variants.implementation_notes: When the other representation is an external encoding, `Codable` is the mapper: declare `private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey` to name the wire keys and implement `init(from:)` / `encode(to:)` only for the parts that need policy (unit conversion, legacy keys, defaults via `decodeIfPresent`), leaving the rest to synthesized conformance. The coding lives with the type, and call sites just use `JSONDecoder` / `JSONEncoder` (`keyDecodingStrategy = .convertFromSnakeCase` covers the mechanical case globally). Choose it when the boundary really is a serialization format; keep a separate mapping initialiser when both sides are in-memory models, because Codable's containers are a poor fit for plain structural conversion.
pitfalls: CodingKeys must list every property you want coded; adding a stored property without updating the enum silently changes what crosses the boundary.
Synthesized conformance fails the whole decode on one bad field: use `decodeIfPresent` and explicit defaults where the producer may omit fields.
Date and Decimal strategies are decoder-level and easy to forget: a mapper that relies on defaults silently changes semantics when another call site uses a different JSONDecoder.
